label: MikroTik cAP-2nD
description: Ceiling access point, single band 2.4 GHz 802.11b/g/n at 300 Mbit/s, one 10/100 Ethernet port with 802.3af PoE in.
notes: Vendor figures from the MikroTik product page specification table: 1x 10/100 Ethernet port, 2.4 GHz max data rate 300 Mbit/s, PoE in 802.3af. **Single band and fast Ethernet** - it cannot take a 5 GHz channel and it cannot saturate a gigabit uplink, so it is not the same lab object as a cAP ac or cAP ax at the same ceiling position.

label: MikroTik GrooveA 52 ac
description: Outdoor airMAX CPE/base station: one gigabit port with passive PoE, 5 GHz 802.11ac radio at 433 Mbit/s, N-connector for an external antenna.
notes: Vendor figures from the MikroTik product page specification table: 1x 10/100/1000 Ethernet port, passive PoE in, 5 GHz max data rate 433 Mbit/s. There is no antenna in the box - the radio has an N-connector, so the link budget depends on whatever is fitted, and a plan that treats the CPE as having integrated gain is wrong.

label: MikroTik RB260GSP
description: Five-port gigabit switch with passive PoE-out and one SFP cage, in a small indoor case.
notes: Vendor figures from the MikroTik product page specification table: 5x 10/100/1000 Ethernet ports, 1x SFP port, passive PoE in - the page describes it as a 'PoE out Ethernet Smart Switch'. The PoE-out here is **passive**, not 802.3af/at: it passes the input voltage through, so a device expecting negotiation will not come up.

label: MikroTik GPERx6 (CSS606)
description: Outdoor Layer-2 switch: 3x gigabit with PoE-out on 2, 3x SFP+, and 802.3bt PoE input.
notes: Vendor figures from the MikroTik product page specification table: 3x 10/100/1000 Ethernet ports with 2 of them PoE-out, 3x SFP+ ports, PoE in 802.3bt. It is powered by PoE *in* while powering other devices on PoE *out*, so the input budget has to cover the downstream load - the spec shows both directions rather than only one.

label: MikroTik wAP ac LTE6 kit
description: Outdoor AP with an embedded LTE6 modem: 2x gigabit, dual-band 802.11ac (300 + 867 Mbit/s), 802.3af PoE in.
notes: Vendor figures from the MikroTik product page specification table: 2x 10/100/1000 Ethernet ports, PoE in 802.3af, wireless 2.4 GHz max data rate 300 Mbit/s and 5 GHz max 867 Mbit/s. The embedded modem is an LTE Cat 6, modelled at the conservative 50 Mbit/s uplink class the catalogue uses for Cat 6 rather than a peak marketing figure.

label: MikroTik Wireless Wire nRAY
description: 60 GHz point-to-point link kit: two nRAY units, each with one gigabit port with 802.3af PoE in and a 60 GHz radio.
notes: Vendor figures from the MikroTik product page specification table: the kit is two nRAY units, 1x 10/100/1000 Ethernet port each, PoE in 802.3af. The 60 GHz radio is modelled at the wired port's 1G - the page gives the band and the port rate but no single maximum for the radio, so treat that figure as unconfirmed.

label: MikroTik wAP LR8 kit
description: LoRaWAN gateway kit: 868 MHz LoRa module, 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi, one 10/100 Ethernet port with PoE in, GPS.
notes: Vendor figures from the MikroTik product page specification table: 10/100 Ethernet ports 1, a 2.4 GHz WiFi interface, an 868 MHz LoRa module and built-in GPS. The LoRa radio is **not** modelled as an interface: the catalogue's interface speeds are of the form 600M or 4.8G, and a LoRa link's rate is orders of magnitude below that, so putting a number there would be a fabricated figure in a field that looks authoritative. The `lora` capability records that the radio exists; plan the 868 MHz side from the LoRaWAN spec rather than from this file.

label: MikroTik Chateau LTE18 ax
description: LTE18 desktop router with Wi-Fi 6: four gigabit ports plus one 2.5G port, SIM slot, 802.11ax dual band.
notes: Vendor figures from the MikroTik product page: 'we kept four Gigabit Ethernet ports and added a 2.5 Gigabit Ethernet' port, plus an LTE modem and Wi-Fi 6. The 2.5G port is modelled at 2.5G rather than 1G because that is the whole point of the model - rounding it down would hide the only fast port on the device.
